source: Let's make a cel-shading 3D game called Gallery. The core loop is paint using a simplified canvas, you're only given 45 seconds, and your canvas you can equip new colors that you've unlocked but can only have 4 available per round. The art you make gets saved and added to a new permanent portrait image in your digital gallery. You can always go up to and inspect these, by walking around in 3D in the gallery then inspecting. The most recent one you make is on a 3D easel at the front of your gallery. Every time you paint a new image with a combination of colors you haven't used before, you get to permanently unlock a new paint color you can use.

image_prompt.text: A 3D easel at the front of the gallery holding the player's most recent painting, composed as the hero focal point of the space
Spawn placed and oriented so a visitor's first view is down the gallery toward the easel, never backstage geometry
framed portrait paintings hung along the gallery walls as a permanent, growing personal collection, spaced far enough apart to walk up to each one
a simplified painting station in the gallery where the player takes up a canvas to paint

layout_placement.text: Spawn point oriented toward the easel composition
Small optional finds tucked off the main gallery floor for visitors who explore further
an inspect trigger at each hung portrait and at the easel so the player can stop and view the art close up

notes: collectible-nodes came in with the preset; the prompt never asks for hidden finds.
The 45-second round, the four-colour equip limit and the colour-unlock rule are UI and progression concerns with no layout footprint.
The wall collection grows permanently over time, so the number of hung frames is not fixed at build time.

open_questions.ask: Cel-shading is a render style rather than a setting - should the gallery read as a clean white-cube museum, a cosy home studio, or something else?
How many finished portraits should the gallery be sized to hold before it has to expand?

coverage_missing.ask: Cel-shading is a render style - what setting should the gallery itself be?
How large a collection should the gallery be sized for?
Is the gallery a private single-player space or can other players walk through it?

answers.ask: Cel-shading is a render style rather than a setting - should the gallery read as a clean white-cube museum, a cosy home studio, or something else?
answers.answer: Make it a clean white-cube museum rendered in cel-shaded 3D, with the easel prominently placed at the front.

answers.ask: How many finished portraits should the gallery be sized to hold before it has to expand?
answers.answer: Size the initial gallery for 12 finished portraits before it expands.
